successors.name: Communist Party of China (Chinese Soviet Republic, Shaan-Gan-Ning Border Region and Liberated Areas)
successors.text: Taiyuan and Datong, the last ground, 'which fell to the Communists in 1949' (the rest of Shanxi had already fallen)

ledger.x: 1911: Yan Xishan takes Shanxi in the Xinhai Revolution.
June 1928: Yan's troops take Beijing and the coast.
6 June 1928: Yan's army enters Beijing as the Nationalist Third Collective Army.
December 1929 (bridging): the Cliopatria row changes from Kuomintang to Republic of China and the Nanjing government continues under the second name; no opened page says anything of Yan in 1929.
1930 (bridging): the Shanxi clique continues as a Nationalist ally under the Republic of China row until the Central Plains War.

May 1930: the Shanxi clique turns against Nanjing in the Central Plains War ('warlord coalitions led by Yan Xishan, Feng Yuxiang, and Li Zongren', May - November 1930; Yan and Feng resigned on 4 November).
20 September 1930: the Northeast Army takes Peking.
30 August 1945: the occupied part of Shanxi returns.

By October 1948 (bridging): the Taiyuan campaign page, opened for the thin item, says that after the Central Shanxi campaign 'the majority of the province had fallen into the communist hands' and the Nationalists 'were left with only Taiyuan and Datong'; the page does not date that campaign or name its towns (it…

ledger.x: 24 April 1949: Taiyuan falls and Yan's Shanxi ends.

wars.name: Northern Expedition
wars.outcome: Kuomintang victory: Yan Xishan 'joined the NRA instead, and drove Fengtian armies from Beijing'; the Shanxi clique was allowed to expand to the sea.

wars.name: Central Plains War
wars.outcome: Nationalist victory: Yan Xishan and Feng Yuxiang resigned on 4 November 1930; the Northeast Army captured Peking in September.

wars.name: Battle of Taiyuan
wars.outcome: Japanese victory: 'part of Suiyuan, most of Shanxi and the NRA arsenal at Taiyuan'.

wars.name: Chinese Civil War (Shanxi front)
wars.outcome: Communist victory: 'the majority of the province had fallen into the communist hands' before the assault, which ran from 5 October 1948 to 24 April 1949; Taiyuan fell on 24 April, Yan having left by air on 5 February.

certainty.note: Shanxi province's boundary is an administrative line; the 1928-1930 Hebei coast, the Shanhai Pass corridor and the 1938-1944 south-western ring are not surveyed and stay soft.
